subject: literature
passage: The brothers had not spoken in four years when their father's will left them his old sailboat jointly, on the condition that it be made seaworthy before it was sold. They met at the boatyard in silence and worked from opposite ends of the hull, Anders scraping paint at the bow and Lars at the stern. By the third Saturday they had reached the middle. <u>Lars held out the sanding block without a word, and Anders, after a moment, took it.</u> They worked side by side until dark, and when they stopped, Anders asked whether Lars still took his coffee black.
stem: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?

choices.A: It depicts a small gesture that signals the start of the brothers' reconciliation.
choices.B: It reveals the reason the brothers stopped speaking to each other four years earlier.
choices.C: It shows that Lars has decided to leave the rest of the work on the boat to Anders.
choices.D: It suggests that the brothers' long quarrel has become more bitter than before.

explanation.why: Before the underlined sentence, the brothers work "in silence" from "opposite ends." In the underlined sentence, one offers a tool and the other accepts it. Afterward they work "side by side," and Anders asks a friendly question. The small exchange marks the start of their reconciliation.
explanation.A: Correct. The silent offer and acceptance of the sanding block leads directly to the brothers working together and talking.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The text never explains the cause of the brothers' silence.
explanation.C: Incorrect. After the exchange the brothers work "side by side," so Lars does not stop working.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The brothers begin cooperating and talking after the exchange, the opposite of growing more bitter.
